  - text: CLASS 10 · TRIGONOMETRY APPLICATIONS
  - heading "Shadow Length Modelling" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Use shadow length and solar elevation to determine object height.
  - text: "Class 10 Trigonometry Applications Level: Intermediate 15–20 min"
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - article:
      - heading "MODEL THE SCENE" [level=2]
      - img
      - text: Same sun, similar triangles
      - img "Interactive object and shadow model":
        - slider "Shadow endpoint"
        - text: "0 Solar elevation (θ) 45.0° Object (vertical) h = 6.00 m θ = 45.0° Shadow length: 6.00 m"
    - complementary:
      - heading "CONTROLS" [level=2]
      - text: Solar elevation (θ)
      - strong: 45.0°
      - slider "Solar elevation": "45"
      - text: 10° 80° Shadow length (s)
      - strong: 6.00 m
      - slider "Shadow length": "6"
      - text: 0.5 m 20 m Units
      - button "m"
      - button "cm"
      - heading "INSTANT RESULT" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Object height (h)
      - strong: 6.00 m
      - paragraph: "Formula: tan θ = h/s"
      - button "Reset":
        - img
        - text: Reset
    - article:
      - heading "SIMILAR TRIANGLE COMPARISON" [level=2]
      - text: Reference (sun) ∿ Your scene
      - paragraph: The same solar angle fixes the same height-to-shadow ratio.
    - article:
      - heading "HEIGHT CALCULATION" [level=2]
      - paragraph: tan θ = h/s
      - paragraph: h = s tan θ
      - paragraph: = 6.00 × tan(45.0°)
      - strong: = 6.00 m
    - article:
      - heading "CHECK" [level=2]
      - paragraph: tan 45.0° = 1.0000
      - paragraph: h/s = 1.0000
      - strong:
        - img
        - text: Ratios agree.
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: WHY IT WORKS
      - paragraph: Sun rays are effectively parallel. The object and its shadow form a right triangle with angle θ.
      - paragraph: Every object measured under the same sun forms a similar right triangle.
      - strong: tan θ = height / shadow length
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISCONCEPTION
      - paragraph: Using a sloped surface as the base breaks the right angle. The model assumes horizontal ground.
      - img "Tree on sloped ground"
      - strong: Keep the base horizontal.
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A vertical pole casts a 6.0 m shadow when solar elevation is 45°. Find its height.
      - paragraph: tan 45° = h/6.0
      - paragraph: h = 6.0 × 1
      - strong: Height = 6.0 m
    - article:
      - heading "REFERENCE STICK" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A 1.5 m stick casts a 2.0 m shadow. Find the solar elevation.
      - paragraph: tan θ = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75
      - strong: θ = 36.87°
    - article:
      - heading "PRACTICE CHALLENGE" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: PRACTICE CHALLENGE
      - paragraph: A tree casts an 8.40 m shadow. A 1.5 m stick casts a 2.00 m shadow at the same time.
      - img "Tree casting an 8.4 metre shadow"
      - text: 8.40 m
      - paragraph: h = 8.40 × (1.5/2.0)
      - strong: Estimated height = 6.30 m
